title: Solar System: Planets and Formation
text: The solar system consists of the Sun and all the objects gravitationally bound to it, including eight planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, and comets. The solar system formed approximately 4.6 billion years ago from the gravitational collapse of a molecular cloud. The four inner planets are rocky; the four outer planets are gas giants (Jupiter, Saturn) and ice giants (Uranus, Neptune). Jupiter is the largest planet with a mass greater than all other planets combined. Saturn is known for its extensive ring system. Pluto was reclassified from planet to dwarf planet by the IAU in 2006.
